A total of 4,768 resonances were detected in 479 plasma discharges during the 2019-2020 JET deuterium campaign.
The resonant frequencies spanned the range f0 ≈ 30-250 kHz, the damping rates were -γ/ω0 ≈ 0-13%, and the toroidal mode numbers were |n| ≤ 30.
The recently upgraded AEAD system allowed probing of high toroidal mode numbers up to |n| ≤ 20, a significant improvement over the previous |n| ≤ 2 capability.
The probability of resonance detection decreased with increasing plasma current and external heating power.
The normalized damping rate increased with edge safety factor but decreased with external heating.
The measured resonant frequencies showed good agreement with the estimated Toroidal Alfvén Eigenmode (TAE) frequencies, with the histogram peaking at a ratio of f0/fTAE = 1.2.
A correction was applied to the measured damping rates to account for the effects of time-varying antenna and resonant frequencies.
The 5th to 95th percentile ranges of plasma parameters were: Ip = 1.0-3.0 MA, B0 = 1.7-3.3 T, and ne0 = 2.5-7.5 × 10^19 m^-3.
The number of resonances detected increased with frequency, with most having f0 ≥ 200 kHz, a typical range for TAEs in JET.

The toroidal mode numbers were estimated using two complementary methods: a weighted chi-square calculation using probe phase information, and the SparSpec algorithm which decomposes both probe amplitude and phase data.
The measured resonant frequencies were generally higher than the estimated TAE frequencies calculated by the MISHKA code, likely due to uncertainties in the safety factor profile.
The predominance of n = 0 mode number estimates could indicate the presence of Global Alfvén Eigenmodes, in addition to potential superposition of modes and limitations in the mode number resolution.
The absolute difference between the applied antenna and estimated resonance mode numbers showed a peak at zero, confirming the successful operation of the AEAD system.
The database included resonances measured in both limiter and X-point magnetic configurations, with approximately 17% and 83% of the total, respectively.

The results from this study provide key information to prepare future experimental campaigns and better understand the physics of Alfvén Eigenmode excitation and damping in the presence of alpha particles.
